newsitem.title: UK: Pakistan hopes for IMF loan approval in early Dec.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan hopes for IMF loan approval in early Dec.

text.p: Pakistan's acting commerce minister said on Thursday he hoped the International Monetary Fund would approve a standby loan to the country early next month.

"There are a number of things needing to be done very quickly. One of them is that we have to reach an agreement with (IMF) fund on the standby programme," Muhammad Zubair Khan told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV).
"We hope that the (IMF) executive board will approve the programme in the first week of December," he added.

Earlier this month, an IMF mission visiting Pakistan after Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's government was dismissed on charges of corruption and misrule, agreed to recommend the reactivation of a $600 million standby loan.
The deal would involve the swift release of two tranches of $80 million to shore up Pakistan's low foreign reserves.
Bhutto denies the charges against her.
